etymology: Pictograph: a person framed squarely inside a carrying-yoke — pinned at the exact middle: center.
mnemonic: Shoulders in the yoke, dead center by definition — オウ. 中央: the middle of the middle.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 黄 (phonetic オウ) — the crossbar laid sideways across the gate: horizontal, side.
mnemonic: The yellow beam bolted crosswise on the frame — よこ. 横浜: the shore that runs sideways along the bay.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 昷 (phonetic オン — read as a covered dish of warm food given kindly) — warmth, in water and in character.
mnemonic: A covered bowl of soup floated to someone who needs it — あたたかい. 温泉: the earth doing the same favor with a whole spring.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person upright (亻) beside a person inverted (匕) — one being flipped into another state: transformation.
mnemonic: Same person, before and after the flip — ばける, カ. 文化 transforms people; 化学 transforms matter; 花 is 化 happening to a plant.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 何 (phonetic カ — itself originally 'to shoulder a load') — the bundle on the shoulder-pole: baggage; also the lotus.
mnemonic: Stalks bound and slung on the pole 何 once pictured — に. 荷物: everything your shoulders answer for.

etymology: Phono-semantic: mound (阝) + 皆 'all' (phonetic カイ) — steps cut up the slope, one for everyone: stairs; a building's floors.
mnemonic: Everybody (皆) climbing the terraced hill one step at a time — カイ. 二階, 三階: the hill moved indoors.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 咸 'all, entire' (phonetic カン) + heart (心) — the heart moved entirely: feeling, sensation.
mnemonic: Not one corner of the heart left dry: total impact — カン. 感じる is when the whole 心 rings at once.

etymology: Phono-semantic: mountain (山) and cliff (厂) + 干 (phonetic ガン) — where high ground breaks off at the water: the shore.
mnemonic: Mountain, then cliff, then the drying line (干) where waves give up — きし. The land's last three strokes before the sea.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 其 (phonetic キ) + moon (月) — time measured by the moon's fixed rounds: a set period, a term.
mnemonic: Mark the calendar by moons: this basket of days is one term — キ. 学期, 期間, 期待: hopes with a due date.

etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 各 'arrive' (phonetic キャク) — the one who arrives under your roof: guest, customer.
mnemonic: Footsteps arriving (各) under your roof: set another place — キャク. お客さん: the arrival you bow to.

etymology: Phono-semantic: jade (王) + 求 (phonetic キュウ) — jade ground into a perfect sphere: a ball, a globe.
mnemonic: Polish the gem until it rolls — たま, キュウ. 野球 sends it flying; 地球 is the one we stand on.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 及 'reach up to' (phonetic キュウ) — threads graded length by length: rank, class.
mnemonic: Silk sorted by how far each strand reaches — キュウ. 上級, 初級: how far up the thread you've climbed.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 喬 'tall, arching' (phonetic キョウ) — timber arched high over the water: a bridge.
mnemonic: Wood bent into a high arc so boats pass under — はし. 日本橋: kilometer zero is a bridge.

etymology: Compound: a body bent (尸) into a cramped compartment — a partitioned room; hence the office, the bureau, and a 'board' situation (結局).
mnemonic: A clerk folded into a cubicle — キョク. 郵便局, 薬局: wherever there's a counter and a queue, there's a 局.

etymology: Pictograph: a bent piece of basketwork or a carpenter's curved ruler — a bend; a melody is a line that bends.
mnemonic: A basket seen edge-on, ribs curving — まがる. Music borrowed it: a 曲 is sound refusing to go straight.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 古 (phonetic ク) — the bitter old herb: bitterness; hence hardship, suffering.
mnemonic: Chew the ancient weed and wince — にがい, くるしい. 苦労: life's aftertaste, prescribed daily.

etymology: Compound ideograph: two hands offering up a vessel — implements presented ready for use: tool, equipment.
mnemonic: Both hands holding up the kit, ready to work — グ. 道具 for the craftsman, 家具 for the home, 具 in your soup: the stuff involved.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand holding the staff of office (尹) + mouth (口) — the one whose word commands: lord; softened into the familiar 'you' and the name-suffix 〜君.
mnemonic: Staff in hand, giving orders — きみ. Time demoted the lord into a schoolboy: 田中君, our young ruler of the classroom.

etymology: Compound: person (亻) + 系 'thread of connection' — the person tied by a thread to a duty: the one in charge.
mnemonic: A thread runs from the task to someone's wrist — かかり. Follow it and you find the 係の人, the person it's tied to.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 夬 'breach' (phonetic ケツ) — the dike cut and the water committed to one channel: to decide.
mnemonic: Break the dam: the water can never un-choose its path — きめる. 決して: 'never', said with the dike already cut.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a drop falling into the ritual dish (皿) — sacrificial blood in the bowl: blood.
mnemonic: One dark drop over the bowl — ち. The dish under it makes it ceremony; the kanji never forgot the altar.

etymology: Compound ideograph: carts (車) parked under a roof (广) — the arsenal and storehouse: warehouse.
mnemonic: Wagons rolled in under one long roof — コ. 冷蔵庫: the household's coldest garage.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 胡 (phonetic コ) — the great still water: a lake.
mnemonic: Water so wide the far shore is a rumor — みずうみ. 琵琶湖: the lake shaped like a lute.

etymology: Pictograph: a house wall with its one window — the direction the window faces: to face, toward, yonder.
mnemonic: The house looks wherever its window does — むかう. 向こう is what the window sees: over there.

etymology: Pictograph of manacles — and the luck of escaping them: good fortune. Happiness, in the oldest script, is the shackle you were spared.
mnemonic: The handcuffs that didn't close on you — しあわせ. 幸せ has always meant: it could have gone otherwise, and didn't.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 巷 'lanes of a town' (phonetic コウ) — streets of water where ships park: a harbor.
mnemonic: The town's alleys continue straight into the sea, boats instead of carts — みなと. 空港: the same alleys, drawn in sky.

etymology: Simplified from 號: a mouth (口) with breath bending out (丂) — a cry, a call; hence a name called out, a numbered designation.
mnemonic: A shout with a hook on it: 'Number 5!' — ゴウ. Trains, typhoons and magazine issues all answer to their 号.

etymology: Phono-semantic: tree (木) + 艮 'fixed, unyielding' (phonetic コン) — the part of the tree that refuses to move: the root.
mnemonic: Pull all you want: the stubborn (艮) part of the tree wins — ね. 大根: the vegetable that is entirely root and pride.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (又) laying meat (月) on the altar (示) — the offering rite: festival.
mnemonic: The offering placed, the drums start — まつり. Every 祭 in Japan is this kanji with lanterns on.

etymology: Phono-semantic: earth (土) + 反 (phonetic ハン) — ground tilted against you: a slope.
mnemonic: The ground pushes back (反) at every step: uphill — さか. 大阪: the big slope that became a big city.

etymology: Pictograph: a shallow dish on its stand, seen from the side — plate, and counter for helpings.
mnemonic: A serving plate drawn in cross-section, food-side up — さら. At the sushi bar you are billed by the stack of 皿.

etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 旨 (phonetic シ) — the hand's pointers: fingers; to point, to indicate.
mnemonic: The part of the hand that knows what it wants (旨) — ゆび. 指す points, 指輪 rings it, 指定 pins the seat.

etymology: Phono-semantic (simplified from 齒): 止 (phonetic シ) over a pictograph of teeth in an open mouth — tooth.
mnemonic: Open wide: rice grains of enamel in their box — は. The 歯医者 is the only person paid to look in there.

etymology: Compound: two (二→冫) + a person pausing open-mouthed (欠) — the second stop, the one after: next.
mnemonic: Catch your breath, then the second leg — つぎ. 次の駅: the station your yawn arrives at.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 弋 'marker stake' + 工 'work' (phonetic シキ) — work done to the staked-out pattern: the set form, a ceremony, a formula.
mnemonic: Stakes out, string taut, everyone follows the pattern — シキ. Weddings (結婚式) and equations (数式) run on the same rails.

etymology: Simplified from 實: a house (宀) strung full of coins (貫) — a filled house: substance; the plant's substance is its fruit; the fact's substance is reality.
mnemonic: The house is actually full — み, the fruit; ジツ, the fact. 実は…: 'here's what's really in the house.'

etymology: Compound ideograph: an ear (耳) in a hand (又) — warriors took the ears of the fallen as proof: to take, grimly literal.
mnemonic: A hand closes on an ear and doesn't let go — とる. Modern life softened it to 取る a photo, 受け取る a parcel.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (寸) under the roof (宀) — the hand that keeps the house: to guard, to keep (a promise).
mnemonic: One hand on the door, all night — まもる. お守り: the shrine sells you that hand, folded in brocade.

etymology: Compound: liquid (氵) + the wine jar (酉, a pictograph of the fermenting vessel) — the jar's liquid: alcohol.
mnemonic: What the ancient jar (酉) sweats out — さけ. 居酒屋: the room built around that jar.

etymology: Compound ideograph: one hand (爫) passing a tray (冖) to another hand (又) — the handover: to receive, accept.
mnemonic: Two hands, one tray, mid-air — うける. 受験 is holding your tray out to an exam board.

etymology: Pictograph: the river (川) with sandbar islets (the dots) — settled sandbanks became districts: province, state.
mnemonic: Three islands anchored in the current — シュウ. 九州: nine of them, grown into a region; アメリカの州: fifty.

etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 合 'fit' (phonetic シュウ) — the hand closing on what it finds: to pick up. Also the formal legal 'ten'.
mnemonic: Hand meets object, perfect fit: yours now — ひろう. On contracts it moonlights as an unforgeable 十.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person (亻) on a mat (百-shaped bedding) under a roof (宀) — a traveler bedded down: lodging, an inn.
mnemonic: One roof, one stranger, one rented futon — やど. 新宿: the 'new inn' that became three million beds; 宿題 the homework you lodge overnight.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 且 (phonetic ジョ) + strength (力) — strength added from the side: to help.
mnemonic: Your load, plus someone else's muscle sliding under it — たすける. 助けて! calls for exactly one more 力.

etymology: Phono-semantic: a phonetic (朕) + strength (力) — strength that lifts and prevails: to win.
mnemonic: Muscle under the load until it rises: victory — かつ. 勝負 pairs this kanji with its shadow, defeat.

etymology: Originally the emblem of the Shang (商) people — after their kingdom fell, they wandered as traders, and their name became the word for commerce.
mnemonic: A whole fallen dynasty setting up market stalls — ショウ. 商売: history's plan B, still in business.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 肖 'shrink, resemble-less' (phonetic ショウ) — doused down to nothing: to extinguish, erase, vanish.
mnemonic: Water on the flame until nothing is left to resemble it — けす. 消しゴム erases pencil; 消える erases anything.
